decision_reason: srppp is an Agroscope-authored, versioned R package with GPL (>=3) source code, installation guidance and an Agroscope scientific publication. Hold pending confirmation that the catalog can cleanly scope the product license to code and explicitly exclude/restrict these bundled data.

decision_reason: The Federal Office of Information Technology, Systems and Telecommunication (FOITT) catalogue identifies this exact jEAP plugin marketplace and lists Apache-2.0, version 0.9.0, stable status, and an August 5 release date. The public repository has Apache-2.0 source and detailed install guidance, but it was created September 9, has only two commits, and has no GitHub release or tag. Hold until the claimed earlier versioned release/artifact or its release provenance can be verified; catalogue fields alone do not establish the release milestone required by the baseline.

government_provenance.note: The Swiss federal catalogue names FOITT, the jEAP team, and this exact repository URL; it describes the plugin marketplace’s role within the federal jEAP platform and lists contact at bit.admin.ch.

public_source.note: The public repository contains the marketplace manifest, plugin source/skills, MCP configuration, installation instructions for multiple coding agents, and an Apache-2.0 license. It is accessible without credentials.

eligible_license.note: The actual repository LICENSE is the standard Apache License 2.0; the first public opensourcing commit includes both this file and product source. Apache-2.0 is OSI-approved.

primary_evidence.note: The catalogue labels the product stable version 0.9.0 with releaseDate 2026-08-05, but the repository itself was created on 2026-09-09 and its Releases API has zero releases and no public tags. README/plugin manifests contain a version string and detailed install steps, but I found no immutable distributable matching the earlier claimed release. Hold pending an auditable release artifact or proof the catalog release date/version is accurate.

decision_reason: This repository is an officially licensed Apache-2.0 example/template archive-type registry, not a standalone software product. Its README explicitly says it is a template/example instance and not application code; real registries are separately created by the business-system teams that own archived data. The FOITT catalog’s version 1.0.0 field does not transform the assigned example repository into an operational product.

public_source.note: The public repository contains Avro schemas, JSON descriptors, Maven build/validation configuration, and documentation. The repository is accessible without credentials.

eligible_license.note: The 2025-09-01 OSS preparation commit adds the standard Apache License 2.0 and identifies the source distribution as Apache-2.0. Apache-2.0 is OSI-approved.

primary_evidence.note: The README says this repository is a “template/example instance” and “not application code”; an actual business-system registry must be created in another repository owned by the relevant teams. It therefore fails product identity/notability as an independent operational or reusable software product, despite its catalog version and schema content.

decision_reason: The FOITT-published Arch Repo Service is a reusable Java library that a jEAP microservice embeds to build and expose a continuously updated architecture inventory. The public repo provides a getting-started guide, running/configuration/operations docs, and versioned releases. Its actual Apache-2.0 grant was added with functional source in the 2025 OSS-preparation commit. The product is a reusable library, not a directly deployable standalone service.

government_provenance.note: The Swiss federal catalog names FOITT, links the exact repository, and describes the jEAP Architecture Repository Service and its purpose. The repository states that it is part of the official jEAP open-source distribution.

public_source.note: The public repository contains Java implementation modules, API/schema documentation, Maven configuration, and a full user/developer/operations guide. Its README makes the exact product boundary clear: this is an embeddable library, not a prebuilt deployable service.

eligible_license.note: The 2025-02-19 OSS-preparation commit adds the Apache License 2.0 alongside the functional Java source and OSS distribution documentation. Current root LICENSE remains the standard Apache License 2.0; Apache-2.0 is OSI-approved.

primary_evidence.note: The README describes architecture inventory functions, Maven dependency integration, versioning/changelog, and links a getting-started guide. The live English FOITT catalog lists software version 15.5.1, release date 2026-09-24. Together these satisfy the agency-published reusable product pathway with a versioned release and installation guidance.

decision_reason: jEAP Audit is a focused, reusable library for building, reliably sending, and consuming standardized audit-record messages in Spring Boot government services. FOITT’s software record identifies the exact library and its 8.12.0 version; the repository provides Maven setup, getting-started, architecture, configuration, sender and consumer guides, versioned changelog, and active tags. The first public Apache-licensed functional source was committed in November 2025.

government_provenance.note: The Swiss federal catalog identifies the Federal Office of Information Technology and Telecommunication, links the exact jeap-admin-ch repository, and describes the audit library for jEAP-based government applications.

public_source.note: The public repository includes source modules for command building, Spring Boot transactional-outbox sending, and command consumption, plus tests and documentation. It is accessible without credentials.

eligible_license.note: The 2025-11-07 public OSS commit adds the standard Apache-2.0 LICENSE with the functional Java implementation; current repo license matches. Apache-2.0 is OSI-approved.

primary_evidence.note: The README documents a reusable audit builder/factory, at-least-once delivery via transactional outbox, consumer support, modules, versioning, and a getting-started installation guide. The live English FOITT catalog lists software version 11.9.0, release date 2026-09-26. Together these meet the agency-published reusable-product pathway.

decision_reason: The jEAP Business Process Test Orchestrator is a reusable library for coordinating end-to-end tests across multiple services, including agent lifecycle, persistence, Zephyr reporting, and test support. The OSS-preparation release commit added Apache-2.0 to the source in 2025.

government_provenance.note: The Swiss federal catalog names FOITT and this exact repository and describes the jEAP Business Process Test Orchestrator as a component coordinating test cases and test agents.

public_source.note: Public Java source includes orchestrator library and instance modules, test-agent client, persistence, reporting, integration/tests, and detailed getting-started/API/configuration docs. The README is explicit that consuming teams build an instance on top of the library rather than running this repository directly.

eligible_license.note: The 2025-01-27 OSS-preparation commit adds the standard Apache License 2.0, publishes documentation and a changelog version, and makes the source distribution explicit. Apache-2.0 is OSI-approved.

primary_evidence.note: The README and linked docs explain integration as a dependency, implementing orchestrator services and test cases, configuration, agent API, test lifecycle, and reporting. The live English FOITT catalog lists software version 18.6.0, release date 2026-09-23. Together these meet the agency-published reusable-library pathway with version and installation guidance.
